source.title: Graph-Guided Selective Unlearning for Language Models: Controlling Support Routes Beyond Forget Seeds
source.authors: Waqas Khan; Tabinda Sarwar; Jing-Yue Cong; Xun Yi; Estrid He

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests leakage under recovery-route prompts after unlearning, using the paper’s graph-guided scope method and a matched seed-only comparison. It does not test the fine-tuning, activation-edit, or quantization attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates fixed direct, paraphrase, indirect, cloze, related-fact, alias, list-summary, and relation-inversion prompts and reports soft leakage. It does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance. Detailed route-level and taxonomy-blind prompt results are reported separately but are not included in rows because the 60-row limit is used for the main method-by-condition table and the matched larger-model comparison.
record.test_reason: A new-method paper (GraphSU) that measures soft leakage of supposedly unlearned facts under fixed direct, paraphrase, alias, cloze, related-fact, list-summary and relation-inversion prompts, plus free-form taxonomy-blind probes. It runs seven baseline unlearning methods and a matched Seed-Only ablation on GPT-2 Medium (TOFU, PISTOL) and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (TOFU). The baseline and Seed-Only results bear on A, whether unlearning removes the knowledge. The GraphSU results bear on F, a newer method resisting prompt-based recovery. Leakage is pooled over all routes, including direct prompts, so it cannot separate rephrasing-driven recovery from plain failure to forget. E is therefore not cleanly tested. There are no fine-tuning, activation-edit or quantization attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that graph-guided expansion of the deletion scope gives the lowest utility-feasible soft leakage in all settings, up to 49.5 points below Seed-Only. They add that results show reduced behavioural reachability under their probes, not certified erasure, and that partial deletion keeps substantial residual leakage.
record.recipe_differences: GraphSU is a graph-guided scope controller paired with local unlearning losses; it is not one of the claim’s fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset, deletion setting, and model. GraphSU’s reduction is smaller for partial deletion; the paper also reports route-family-specific differences, but those values are not extracted as rows here.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
record.problems: The paper reports one training seed. Main benchmark table values have no uncertainty estimates. Soft leakage measures behavioural recovery only under the paper’s probe families and is not a test of representational erasure; there is no chance-level comparison.
record.rows_left_out: The 21 route-family reductions in Figure 2, taxonomy-blind probe comparisons in Appendix F/Table 8, local-extractor result in Appendix D, and separate utility metrics are not included. The 60-row limit is filled by the main method-by-condition leakage table and matched Seed-Only/GraphSU results for Llama 3.2 3B Instruct.

untested.parts: No accuracy against chance or against a never-trained model. No separate direct-prompt result for baselines, so 'forgotten under direct query' is never established.
No activation ablation or internal analysis of blocking versus deletion.
Rephrasing and alias routes are pooled with direct prompts. Per-route leakage levels are not reported, only GraphSU-minus-Seed reductions. No jailbreaks, other languages or in-context attacks.
GraphSU is tested only against prompt routes, not against fine-tuning, activation edits or quantization. Only one training seed.

missing.what: Original-SFT, the pre-unlearning model, has soft leakage 91.25% and hard leakage 37.67% on TOFU complete deletion. This is the only no-unlearning reference, and most baselines do not go below it.
Leakage for the seven baseline methods on Llama-3.2-3B TOFU. For example, entity deletion: GA 36.00, GA+KL 38.66, DPO 92.22, GRU 86.33; complete deletion: 90–99.7%.
Taxonomy-blind free-form probes on TOFU complete deletion: Seed-Only 74.18% against GraphSU 61.68% (fixed-reference detector); confirmed-attack panel 78.95% against 65.20%.
Route-level reductions for GraphSU against Seed-Only (TOFU GPT-2), 17.5–55.0 points per route. Absolute per-route leakage is not reported.
Local-Qwen extractor variant of GraphSU: soft leakage 49.83%, hard leakage 1.33%.

record.verdict_notes: The record's version codes V1/V5/V6 were invalid and are remapped. Baseline and Seed-Only rows now link to A; GraphSU rows link to F. E is not credited: soft leakage pools direct and rephrased prompts, and Original-SFT leakage is 91.25%. High baseline leakage therefore shows failed forgetting, not prompt-driven recovery of apparently forgotten knowledge. The record's E 'supports' label is withdrawn. Baselines were tuned by the authors, and checkpoint selection may not favour them. All results come from one training seed. The peer-review venue in the record cannot be verified from the text.

versions.untested_parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy or chance reference is reported; the study does not test whether attack recovery is no more than on a model that never saw the knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or internal edit to restore knowledge, and no test of whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting.

Tests fixed recovery-route prompts, including paraphrase and alias prompts. Does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information as recovery attacks, and does not compare prompt-only recovery against an unlearned model that never saw the knowledge.
Tests GraphSU against recovery-route prompts only. Does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits, or quantization.

relation.reason: Its own leakage results bear on F (GraphSU) and its baseline runs bear on A.

tranche.reason: Different method (soft leakage under paraphrase, alias, cloze, related-fact and relation-inversion prompts) aimed at the same question: whether unlearned knowledge stays reachable. Proposes GraphSU as a counter-method (F) and runs seven baselines (A).

source_check.notes: The Llama Appendix A tables lose their headers in extraction. The order complete, entity, partial is confirmed by the DPO partial values the text gives (leakage 96.36%, PPL 1.03). The 91.25% Original-SFT leakage is GPT-2 TOFU complete only. All runs use a single training seed, with no CIs except Table 8. The authors claim reduced reachability, not certified erasure, and test only prompt-route attacks.

statements.correction: Soft leakage %, Seed-Only -> GraphSU: GPT-2 TOFU complete 93.25->46.83, entity 96.25->54.60, partial 100->81.67; GPT-2 PISTOL complete 56.33->6.83, entity 26.33->4.67, partial 41.39->29.17; Llama-3.2-3B TOFU complete 93.67->13.33, entity 25.11->15.53, partial 94.33->87.01 (AltPO 88.67, GA+KL 89.00, NPO-TR 89.66). GPT-2 TOFU complete: GRU 38.13 at retain PPL 79.11 vs GraphSU 46.83 at PPL 3.27. Test is recovery-route prompt leakage (embedding-similarity soft leakage), not relearning or RWKU. Verdict for these cases is limits_scope, not challenges.
statements.problem: Cites GraphSU, labelled challenges, as a new method no better than its base or a baseline. The listed conditions (relearning, MUSE, RWKU) don't apply to it. GraphSU beats its matched base (Seed-Only) in all 9 settings and beats every baseline on 2 of the 4 cited rows (GPT-2 TOFU entity and partial). Only Llama TOFU partial (a marginal edge) and GPT-2 TOFU complete (GRU leaks less but collapses utility) fit.
